newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Over 50 killed in Sri Lanka fighting.
newsitem.headline: Over 50 killed in Sri Lanka fighting.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops on Tuesday cleared mines and booby-traps from a northern town just captured from Tamil Tiger fighters during a major government drive into rebel-held territory.
"Troops are clearing parts of the town of booby-traps and mines and consolidating their gains," said one military official in the north.

Military officials said troops took Puliyankulam, some 22 km (14 miles) north of the government-held town of Vavuniya in the heart of the rebels' northern Wanni stronghold, after fierce fighting in which more than 50 soldiers and rebels were killed.
Vavuniya, gateway to the Wanni area controlled by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, is some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.
The Defence Ministry on Tuesday said only that troops were closing in on Puliyankulam and that they had overcome resistance from the rebels.
Thirteen soldiers and one officer were killed on Monday as the rebels tried to slow down advancing troops. At least 24 soldiers were wounded in the fighting, a ministry statement said on Tuesday.
"Troops on the ground confirm that 40 terrorists were killed and more than 70 were wounded," it added.
The LTTE's spokesman in London was not immediately available for comment.
But a rebel statement received on Tuesday said the army continued to bombard Puliyankulam with artillery. It said the town was deserted.
Two weeks ago, the rebels mounted a surprise attack on the military's rear near Vavuniya, delaying the main offensive.
Some 20,000 troops launched the offensive last month to open a crucial highway linking Vavuniya with the Jaffna peninsula, a further 100 km (60 miles) north.
Jaffna city was controlled by the rebels for nearly a decade before being captured by government forces last year.
The rebels, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east, have now set up base in the Wanni.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
